## Body

# Review of #342

Head: df1a9d9ef6da21d019b8588b381417b0d5a97604

**Verdict: BLOCK** for R342-F001 and R342-F002, both introduced wrong-allocation behavior. One review round: the author fixes; the prime verifies the fix commits.

## Findings

**R342-F001 -- directory-stat errors become successful allocations**

`crates/daemon/src/http/claims.rs:829-833`: `entry.path().is_dir()` returns false on metadata errors. A readable but non-searchable `docs/project` can therefore be enumerated, but its existing `prds` directory is silently skipped. In the isolated HTTP fixture, `prds/001-demo.dd.json` exists, the parent has mode 0400, parent enumeration succeeds, and stat fails. The response is nevertheless success with floor 0 and number 001, colliding with the existing document. Main's allocation scan refuses the unreadable directory instead.

Propagate metadata failures through the existing scan-refusal path; skip a matching entry only when its metadata establishes that it is not a directory. Add a regression that restores permissions before asserting and proves both the real metadata failure and that no claim was booked.

**R342-F002 -- generic kinds ending in `s` scan an unrelated name**

`crates/core/src/claims.rs:156-160`, with `seed_folders` at lines 129-134: unknown kinds already supply both their literal name and that name plus `s`. Applying `strip_suffix('s')` to the literal seed also admits a third name. For `status`, the scan accepts `statu`, not just `status` and `statuss`. The isolated fixture with `status/003-own` and `statu/099-other` returns 100 rather than 004.

Keep generic matching to the existing `<kind>` / `<kind>s` pair, case-insensitively; do not strip the literal kind's suffix again. Retain singular/plural support for the known folder table.

## Nonblocking follow-up

`crates/core/src/claims.rs:192-215` and `crates/daemon/src/http/claims.rs:400-403`: the delivered-path reader still uses exact folder prefixes. This is a real normal-use bookkeeping problem, not harmless: an uppercase PRD claim remains open after its merge. The isolated HTTP fixture confirms claim 091 remains open after an uppercase-path delivery while a lowercase-path delivery releases 092. The next claim remains 092 after the first delivery, so it does not reuse 091. This was explicitly excluded from the approved fix; it does not independently block this PR.

Worth proposing to Jordan under C35: align delivered-path recognition with the approved folder spellings, so merges close the claims they actually deliver; pure path matching adds no launches, polls or timers.

## Correctness and cost

Decorated names (`prdx`, `my-prd`, `PRDs-archive`), a nested `old/prd`, non-ASCII lookalikes and a file named `PRD` are excluded. All known folder-scanning kinds, the archive's final segment and a generic kind passed the additional isolated case tests. C29 retains canonical `workstream` store keys for both `workstream` and `roadmap`; the existing mixed-case HTTP regression passes.

This scan is a **POLICY**, not a brake: it determines the allocation floor. The maximum aggregation is monotonic for successfully read folders, but that does not excuse either reading the wrong kind or suppressing errors.

Cost is command-triggered, with no ongoing loop, poll, timer, hook, new process launch or per-seat tick work: one parent `read_dir` per seed, one stat per name-matching entry, and one shallow `read_dir` per directory spelling. The existing root readability read remains. Sorting is per-command O(M log M) in matching spellings; entry enumeration is uncapped but nonrecursive. No live-daemon before/after measurement applies to an unchanged idle path, and no real-project claim or bounce was run.

## Security and privacy

No vulnerabilities or private account names, emails or machine paths were found in the committed diff. Directory symlinks (including parent symlinks) can leave the repository, as before; the new spellings widen that existing read scope. The scan reads immediate entry names and numeric prefixes, not file contents, and never recursively descends, so a cycle cannot cause recursive traversal. This is depth-bounded, not entry-count-bounded or repository-confined. Matching names are restricted to ASCII seed spellings; no discovered arbitrary name is interpolated into an executable repair argument.

## Regression oracles

Append these to the existing isolated `crates/daemon/tests/claims_http.rs` fixture. They exercise only its fake project, store and HTTP server, never the real daemon:

```rust
#[tokio::test]
async fn review342_main_regression_generic_kind_ending_s_does_not_scan_another_kind() {
    let rig = rig("pij-review342-status", Vec::new()).await;
    std::fs::create_dir_all(rig.main.join("docs/project/status/003-own")).unwrap();
    std::fs::create_dir_all(rig.main.join("docs/project/statu/099-other")).unwrap();
    let result = rig
        .call(CODER, "/v1/claim", &["claim", "status", "--for", "own"])
        .await;
    assert_eq!(result["data"]["number"], 4, "{result}");
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn review342_main_regression_stat_failure_refuses_without_claiming() {
    use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;

    let rig = rig("pij-review342-stat", Vec::new()).await;
    let parent = rig.main.join("docs/project");
    let permissions = std::fs::metadata(&parent).unwrap().permissions();
    std::fs::set_permissions(&parent, std::fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o400)).unwrap();
    let parent_readable = std::fs::read_dir(&parent).is_ok();
    let stat_failed = std::fs::metadata(parent.join("prds")).is_err();
    let result = rig
        .call(CODER, "/v1/claim", &["claim", "prd", "--for", "must refuse"])
        .await;
    std::fs::set_permissions(&parent, permissions).unwrap();
    assert!(parent_readable && stat_failed, "permission control");
    assert_eq!(result["ok"], false, "{result}");
    assert_eq!(result["details"]["code"], "E-RS-CLAIM-SCAN", "{result}");
    assert!(rig.store.claims("demo").await.unwrap().is_empty());
}
```
